title: 351. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Properties of Trapezoids
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the defining property of a trapezoid.
questions.question: Using the exclusive convention (which excludes parallelograms), which statement defines a trapezoid?

options.label: A
options.text: A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of opposite sides parallel.

options.label: B
options.text: A quadrilateral with two pairs of opposite sides parallel.

questions.explanation: A trapezoid is defined as a quadrilateral that has exactly one pair of opposite sides parallel. The other pair of opposite sides is not parallel. Option B describes a parallelogram, not a trapezoid.
questions.hint: Recall how many pairs of opposite sides are parallel in a trapezoid.

questions.concept: Bases and Legs of a Trapezoid
questions.learningObjective: Identify the legs of a trapezoid given its parallel sides.
questions.question: In trapezoid \(ABCD\), \(AB \parallel CD\). Which sides are the legs of the trapezoid?
questions.explanation: In a trapezoid, the parallel sides are called the bases, and the non-parallel sides are called the legs. Since \(AB \parallel CD\), the bases are \(AB\) and \(CD\). Therefore, the legs are \(AD\) and \(BC\).
questions.hint: The legs are the sides that are not parallel.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a property of the base angles of an isosceles trapezoid.
questions.question: In an isosceles trapezoid, which statement is true?

options.label: B
options.text: Each pair of base angles are equal.

questions.explanation: An isosceles trapezoid has equal legs. A key property is that each pair of base angles is equal. Perpendicular diagonals are not a general property of an isosceles trapezoid.
questions.hint: Recall which angles are equal in an isosceles trapezoid.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the length relationship for the median of a trapezoid.
questions.question: The median of a trapezoid is parallel to the bases. Its length is equal to which expression?

options.label: A
options.text: Half the difference of the bases.

options.label: B
options.text: Half the sum of the bases.

questions.explanation: The median (midsegment) of a trapezoid is parallel to the bases and its length is half the sum of the two bases. If the bases have lengths \(b_1\) and \(b_2\), the median length is \(\frac{1}{2}(b_1+b_2)\).
questions.hint: Recall how the median length combines the two bases.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the median length given the two bases.
questions.question: A trapezoid has bases of length \(8\text{ cm}\) and \(12\text{ cm}\). What is the length of its median?
questions.explanation:
The median length is half the sum of the bases:
\[
\frac{1}{2}(8+12)=\frac{1}{2}\times 20=10\text{ cm}.
\]
Therefore, the median is \(10\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Add the two bases, then divide by \(2\).

questions.concept: Finding a Base from the Median
questions.learningObjective: Determine an unknown base using the trapezoid median formula.
questions.question: A trapezoid has median length \(9\text{ cm}\) and one base length \(6\text{ cm}\). What is the length of the other base?
questions.explanation:
Let the other base be \(x\). The median formula gives
\[
9=\frac{1}{2}(6+x).
\]
Multiplying both sides by \(2\) gives \(18=6+x\), so \(x=12\). Therefore, the other base is \(12\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Set the median equal to half the sum of the two bases.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the formula for the area of a trapezoid.
questions.question: Which formula gives the area of a trapezoid with bases \(b_1\), \(b_2\), and height \(h\)?
questions.explanation:
The area of a trapezoid is half the product of the height and the sum of the bases:
\[
A=\frac{1}{2}(b_1+b_2)h.
\]
Option B is not a valid area formula for a trapezoid.
questions.hint: Recall how the height and the two bases combine in the area formula.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a property of the diagonals of an isosceles trapezoid.
questions.question: In an isosceles trapezoid, which statement about the diagonals is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The diagonals are equal in length.

options.label: B
options.text: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles.

questions.explanation: A property of an isosceles trapezoid is that its diagonals are congruent. They are not generally perpendicular, and they do not generally bisect each other at right angles.
questions.hint: Recall which diagonal property holds for every isosceles trapezoid.

questions.concept: Base Angles of an Isosceles Trapezoid
questions.learningObjective: Calculate a base angle using the equal base angle property.
questions.question: In isosceles trapezoid \(ABCD\), \(AB \parallel CD\), and \(\angle A=70^\circ\). What is \(\angle B\)?
questions.explanation:
In an isosceles trapezoid, the base angles at the same base are equal. Since \(AB \parallel CD\), \(\angle A\) and \(\angle B\) are base angles at base \(AB\). Therefore,
\[
\angle B=\angle A=70^\circ.
\]
questions.hint: Use the equal base angles property at the same base.

questions.concept: Finding a Base from the Median
questions.learningObjective: Solve for an unknown base using the median formula.
questions.question: A trapezoid has median length \(10\text{ cm}\) and one base length \(7\text{ cm}\). What is the length of the other base?
questions.explanation:
Let the other base be \(x\). The median formula gives
\[
10=\frac{1}{2}(7+x).
\]
Multiplying both sides by \(2\) gives \(20=7+x\), so \(x=13\). Therefore, the other base is \(13\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Use the median formula and solve for the unknown base.
